Use case: stylized-concept. Production asset for a photorealistic medieval TOP DOWN strategy game.
Input image 1 is the EXISTING ROCK TILE style, scale, edge treatment and lighting reference. Input image 2 is the IRON MINE material reference only. Generate a NEW standalone rock cluster, NOT a building or mine.
Strict camera: VERTICAL NADIR, orthographic straight-down aerial texture. No isometric view, no horizon, no tilted ground plane. Rocks may have relief seen through crags and short contact shadows, but the camera looks straight down.
Subject: dark charcoal-grey iron-bearing crags, steeper jagged ridges and tight fractured slate, small subtle rusty mineral seams. Darker than the reference but still readable, NOT black obsidian or fantasy crystals.
Variant 1: three medium fractured masses with broken smaller pieces and irregular gaps.
Compatibility: same physical rock scale and detailed realistic weathered material as reference1; neutral medium-grey transitional rubble at the irregular edges, tiny sparse olive moss, short soft shadows towards lower right with diffuse light from upper left. Border pieces become smaller with a ragged alpha contour, no square tile edge, no opaque grass patch. Cluster fills about 85% of a square canvas, comfortably inside frame with fully transparent margin on every side. It will overlap adjacent normal rocks and other variants repeatedly, so no iconic unique centerpiece, no dramatic long shadow, no huge standalone mountain peak.
Output: a single high resolution RGBA rock-cluster cutout on TRUE TRANSPARENT background, at least1024 pixels each side. No text, labels, border, buildings, tools, rails, people, or equipment.
